instruction: I'm working up a marketing visual for a high-end heritage property, meant for the online listing that goes in front of the owner and prospective buyers, so the whole point is to make the space feel bright, open and impressive enough to win them over. Please recreate the neo-Gothic cathedral-hall interior shown on the phone screen: a run of ribbed cross vaults with pointed-arch arcades receding in depth, clustered stone columns carrying the ribs on both sides, a marble staircase with an ornate dark-red wrought-metal balustrade dropping to a lower level, and a chandelier hanging above—keep this layout and the bay/depth and ceiling-height proportions exactly as in the image, don't change them. Then float two spheres mid-corridor as AR elements: a larger iridescent soap-bubble one (thin-film/oil-slick interference, semi-transparent, view-dependent color shift) and a smaller matte magenta solid one, one behind the other. For materials, use warm off-white sandstone/marble PBR on the walls, columns and vaults (subtle bump and aged grime), dark-red painted metal with gold trim on the railing, and brass with warm-white glowing bulbs for the chandelier. Light it warm indoors, chandelier as key with daylight spilling in from the far end of the arcade as fill, for soft global illumination and graded vault shadows. Two things matter most: the natural light coming in at the far end has to read bright and airy, not gloomy, and the overall bay/depth and the staircase scale need to feel believable at a glance. Perspective camera roughly matching the shot in the image—looking down the arcade with the staircase low in frame. Render in Cycles, physically correct materials, denoising on, give me a 3840x2160 PNG with Filmic color management, and save the .blend too, collections named by vaults, columns, staircase & railing, chandelier and spheres. Judge sizes from the proportions in the image and set the finer details yourself—no exact millimeters needed.
